newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK AIMS TO SELL ITS BANK IN FOUR MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK AIMS TO SELL ITS BANK IN FOUR MONTHS.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland, the central bank, wants to sell the last commercial bank it owns, the Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank w Lublinie SA, in the next four months, an NBP press office official said.

Krzysztof Mielnicki told Reuters the NBP wanted to conclude the deal before Poland's new constitution is in force, because under the constitution the sale of NBP property would be regulated by a separate law, which has not been created yet.
"NBP's deputy president Witold Kozinski said yesterday at a meeting with heads of the bank's branches that the NBP wants to sell Pierwszy Komercyjny in the next four months," he said.
Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank w Lublinie, fully owned by the NBP, has 39 branches, a balance sheet total of 1.7 billion zlotys and own assets 173 million zlotys.

It made a net loss of 9.1 million zlotys in 1996. It was taken over by the NBP in 1993 after it fell into financial problems a year earlier when its owner, a U.S. citizen David Bogatin, was extradited to the United States for financial crimes commited there.
